PCCP.name: FDA PCCP Guidance (Dec 2024)
PCCP.what_it_teaches: Manufacturers must specify planned modifications, methodology to develop/validate/implement them, and impact assessment. Applies across 510(k)/De Novo/PMA.
PCCP.relevance_to_MSVED: Creates the REQUIREMENT for minimum sufficient evidence — every PCCP must determine what validation each modification needs.

ISO14971.name: ISO 14971 Risk Management / FMEA
ISO14971.what_it_teaches: Risk-based V&V proportional to residual risk. Hazard analysis, risk estimation, risk control, residual risk evaluation.
ISO14971.relevance_to_MSVED: Provides the risk-envelope framework. Link 2 (risk-envelope propagation) is ISO 14971 applied to ML changes.

InfluenceFunctions.name: ML Change-Impact Analysis (influence functions, datamodels)
InfluenceFunctions.what_it_teaches: Maps which training data points / subpopulations a model change affects. Koh & Liang (2017), datamodels (Ilyas et al.).
InfluenceFunctions.relevance_to_MSVED: Provides link 1's ML-side analysis. But maps to TRAINING DATA, not CLINICAL PATHWAYS.

BOED.name: Bayesian Optimal Experiment Design
BOED.what_it_teaches: Selects experiments that maximally reduce posterior uncertainty / distinguish hypotheses. Foster, Ivanova, Rainforth et al.
BOED.relevance_to_MSVED: Closest to link 3. But optimizes INFORMATION GAIN, not SAFETY SUFFICIENCY.

ActiveTesting.name: Active Testing / Active Evaluation
ActiveTesting.what_it_teaches: Selects most informative samples to estimate performance with fewer labels. Kossen et al., Farquhar/Gal.
ActiveTesting.relevance_to_MSVED: Also close to link 3. But optimizes ESTIMATION ACCURACY, not safety sufficiency.

NI_testing.name: Non-Inferiority Statistical Testing
NI_testing.what_it_teaches: Tests whether a new version is 'not worse' than the old by a pre-defined margin Δ. ICH E9. Standard in clinical trials.
NI_testing.relevance_to_MSVED: Provides the statistical framework for link 4's sufficiency argument. But is a single hypothesis test, not a full sufficiency proof.

AssuranceCases.name: Assurance Cases / Goal Structuring Notation (GSN)
AssuranceCases.what_it_teaches: Structured argument for why evidence is sufficient to support a safety claim. DO-178C, ISO 26262. Hawkins, Graydon, Matsuno.
AssuranceCases.relevance_to_MSVED: Provides the STRUCTURE for link 4's sufficiency proof. But manually authored, not ML-specific, not tied to minimum-evidence derivation.

ConformalPAC.name: Conformal Prediction / PAC Bounds / Risk Control
ConformalPAC.what_it_teaches: Distribution-free coverage guarantees. Bates, Angelopoulos et al. 'Risk control' — controlling a risk functional with guarantees.
ConformalPAC.relevance_to_MSVED: Provides STATISTICAL GUARANTEES for link 4. But population-level, not modification-specific evidence-set sufficiency.

verdict.the_question: Would a PHOSITA (at the intersection of ML, regulatory science, and clinical safety) have been motivated to combine these components to derive a safety-sufficient minimum evidence set for an ML modification, with a reasonable expectation of success?
verdict.the_honest_answer: MSVED is MARGINAL TO WEAK under §103. The motivation is STRONG (PCCP requires it). Each component is individually known. The 4-link chain maps to PCCP's own structure. Under KSR v. Teleflex, combining known components to solve a problem that the market is explicitly asking for is likely obvious.

link_1_clinical_bridge.description: The bridge from ML model change → CLINICAL pathways (not just training data subpopulations). No existing tool performs this bridge. Influence functions map to training data; clinical pathway modeling is separate.
link_1_clinical_bridge.novelty_strength: MARGINAL — the bridge is engineering, not invention. A PHOSITA would say 'connect influence functions to a clinical ontology.'
link_1_clinical_bridge.survives_section_103: UNCERTAIN — depends on whether the bridge requires a non-obvious intermediate representation.

link_3_safety_objective.description: Reframing BOED/active testing from 'information gain' to 'safety sufficiency within a risk envelope.' The objective function is different.
link_3_safety_objective.novelty_strength: WEAK — reframing an existing optimization objective is likely obvious. FDA's 'least burdensome' mandate already points this way.
link_3_safety_objective.survives_section_103: NO — this is an objective-function reframing, not a new mechanism.

link_4_modification_specific_sufficiency.description: An automated, modification-specific, clinical-risk-aware sufficiency proof that is tied to the DERIVED minimum evidence set (not just a population-level bound).
link_4_modification_specific_sufficiency.novelty_strength: MARGINAL — assurance cases + conformal/PAC together cover the structure and guarantees. But tying them to a DERIVED minimum set for a SPECIFIC modification is not directly taught.
link_4_modification_specific_sufficiency.survives_section_103: UNCERTAIN — depends on whether the proof technique is a novel theorem or just an integration of known methods.

what_does_not_survive.the_full_chain: The 4-link chain as a whole is likely obvious. PCCP provides motivation, each link is individually known, and the combination is predictable. 'Obvious to try' under KSR.
what_does_not_survive.link_2_risk_propagation: ISO 14971 FMEA is standard. Automating it from an ML change is engineering, not invention.

verdict.kill_or_survive: CONDITIONAL_SURVIVE — MSVED survives ONLY if link 1's clinical bridge or link 4's modification-specific sufficiency proof contains a non-obvious technical element. The full chain as an 'integrated system' is likely obvious.
verdict.survival_condition: MSVED must demonstrate a TECHNICAL EFFECT that is NOT predictable from the components. Specifically: the killer experiment (P2) must show that MSVED produces a DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than (a) BOED-optimal, (b) expert risk-based, or (c) conventional fixed plans — with the SAME assurance coverage. If MSVED = BOED + risk reframing (predictable), it is obvious. If MSVED produces materially different evidence sets due to the clinical pathway bridge, it may survive.
verdict.implication: The §103 attack does NOT cleanly kill MSVED, but it does NOT clear it either. MSVED is in a CONDITIONAL state: it survives only if the killer experiment demonstrates a non-obvious technical effect. If the killer experiment shows MSVED = BOED + risk reframing, MSVED is killed.

p2_killer_experiment.honest_label: This is a SYNTHETIC test of the MECHANISM, not buyer validation. It tests whether MSVED produces a different/better evidence set than alternatives. It does NOT prove buyer value.

candidates.name: MSVED (Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation)
candidates.buyer: AI/ML medical-device companies with PCCP obligations
candidates.existing_workflow: Manual risk assessment + full re-validation per modification
candidates.smallest_mechanism: The 4-link chain (change → pathway → risk → min evidence → proof)
candidates.technical_effect: Same assurance, fewer tests (P2 result: D uses fewer tests than C/BOED with similar assurance)
candidates.validation_route: Killer experiment PASS (synthetic). Next: external validation on real PCCP data.
candidates.ip_attack: §103 MARGINAL — full chain likely obvious. Survival depends on clinical-pathway bridge being non-obvious.
candidates.build_vs_buy: 4 rare skill sets (clinical + risk + BOED + assurance). 12-24 months internal. $500K-$2M.

candidates.name: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator
candidates.buyer: Regulatory affairs teams at AI-device companies
candidates.smallest_mechanism: Automated, modification-specific sufficiency proof (link 4 of MSVED)
candidates.validation_route: Generate proof for 2-3 modifications, have regulatory expert assess
candidates.ip_attack: Link 4 is the RAREST element. Assurance case automation exists but not ML-specific + not tied to derived minimum evidence.
candidates.build_vs_buy: Formal methods + assurance + ML. Very rare. 9-18 months.

candidates.name: Clinical Pathway Change-Impact Mapper
candidates.smallest_mechanism: Bridge from ML change → clinical pathways (link 1)
candidates.technical_effect: Maps model delta to clinical decision points
candidates.validation_route: Map changes for 2-3 published modifications with known clinical impacts
candidates.ip_attack: Link 1→2 is the LEAST CONTESTED gap. No prior art bridges ML change to clinical pathways.
candidates.build_vs_buy: Clinical ontology + ML change-impact. Niche. 6-12 months.

candidates.name: PCCP Modification Bound-Checker
candidates.smallest_mechanism: Formal verification of modification within PCCP boundaries
candidates.ip_attack: NOT covered by existing PCCP tools. Must verify no formal methods work.

candidates.name: Evidence Chain-of-Custody for FDA Inspection
candidates.validation_route: Build chain for 2-3 modification cycles, QA expert assessment
candidates.ip_attack: eQMS does document management but not tamper-evident ML evidence chains.

candidates.name: Subgroup Regression Detector
candidates.existing_workflow: Bias testing tools (AIF360, Fairlearn) — test once, not across modifications
candidates.smallest_mechanism: Paired subgroup analysis with power calculation across versions
candidates.validation_route: Apply to 2-3 published modifications with known subgroup impacts
candidates.ip_attack: Bias tools exist but don't do paired regression across modifications.

candidates.name: Non-Inferiority Statistical Engine
candidates.smallest_mechanism: Automated paired NI comparison with pre-registered margins
candidates.validation_route: Apply to 2-3 modifications with known NI outcomes
candidates.ip_attack: NI testing is standard (ICH E9). Automation + ML packaging is the novelty. Moderate collision risk.
candidates.build_vs_buy: Biostatistics + ML. 3-6 months. Modest build cost.

candidates.name: Clinical Risk Model Propagator
candidates.smallest_mechanism: Auto-propagation of ML change through clinical risk model (link 2)
candidates.validation_route: Propagate 2-3 changes through published risk model
candidates.ip_attack: ISO 14971 FMEA is standard but manual. Auto-propagation from ML is novel.

candidates.name: Modification Impact Assessor for PCCP
candidates.buyer: Regulatory teams writing PCCP impact assessments
candidates.smallest_mechanism: Quantitative impact prediction from model change
candidates.validation_route: Predict impact for 2-3 modifications with known outcomes
candidates.ip_attack: Impact assessment required by PCCP but no tool automates quantitatively.

candidates.name: Safety-Sufficient Subset Selector (vs BOED)
candidates.existing_workflow: BOED / active testing (optimizes info gain, not safety)
candidates.technical_effect: Minimum test set where passing = safety proven
candidates.validation_route: Compare safety-sufficient vs BOED-optimal on same dataset
candidates.ip_attack: HIGHEST collision risk. Must prove safety-sufficient ≠ BOED reframing.
candidates.build_vs_buy: Formal safety spec + subset optimization. 6-9 months.
